slides: Open by explaining that submanifolds are where the rank technology from the previous chapter becomes geometry inside an ambient manifold. The chapter asks when a subset or image deserves its own smooth structure, tangent spaces, restricted maps, and boundary charts.

Use the route slide to separate the chapter's tests. Students should watch for embedded versus immersed behavior, local slice and level-set criteria, tangent spaces as kernels, restriction gates for maps, boundary half-slices, and parameter values where rank drops.

The roadmap slide keeps the criteria visible. A subset becomes a usable submanifold only after local coordinates, topology, and tangent-space behavior line up. The final checks say the roadmap dependency graph is acyclic, so the criteria are ordered rather than circular.

This slide clarifies why immersed and embedded submanifolds cannot be conflated. The figure-eight has sampled nonzero speed but still creates a global topology issue, while parabola and singular zero-set examples show how regularity and smoothness can separate.

The sphere slice is the clean regular level-set example. At the north pole, the gradient of rho has rank one, tangent basis vectors kill the gradient, and a local graph z equals square root of one minus x squared minus y squared gives a slice chart.

Tangent spaces inside an ambient tangent space can be tested by killing defining functions. On the circle sample, the tangent vector is orthogonal to the gradient, the symbolic gradient dot velocity is zero, and the numeric residual is exactly zero.

Map restriction is a topology gate, not just notation. Restricting the domain is automatic for immersed or embedded submanifolds, but restricting the codomain through an immersed submanifold needs an extra continuity hypothesis; embedded codomains get that gate from the subspace topology.

Boundary submanifolds add a half-space test. At a boundary point of the closed disk, the defining derivative separates inward, outward, and tangent directions, so local coordinates model the submanifold by an ordinary slice inside a half-space.

The rank-drop lab makes the regular value condition dynamic. The family x squared minus y squared minus epsilon has a critical point at the origin, but that critical point lies on the zero level only when epsilon is zero, which is the singular parameter.

Close by tying the chapter back to constant-rank ideas. Submanifolds are not just subsets; they are subsets with local models, compatible topology, tangent spaces, and restriction behavior that survive the checks. The next chapters use those habits for Sard and transversality.
